text: Eleven fifty-nine. The city is asleep. Your phone isn't.
asr: 11.59. The city is asleep. Your phone isn't.

text: At midnight, it updates, like it always does.
Except tonight, the news is dated tomorrow.
Most of it is ordinary. The weather. The trams. A lost dog.
You laugh, and go to sleep.
Seven forty-one. The sky is dry.
Seven forty-two.
Real forecasters can't do this. Even with supercomputers, their forecasts gain only about one day of accuracy every ten years.
Yours is perfect. Down to the minute.
Every headline comes true. The late tram. The lost dog on Mill Street. The final score.
For one whole morning, you know everything a day early.
Then, at noon, a new headline.
Rosa. Your heater. Unplug it. Please.
That old thing? It's kept me warm for twenty years.
Not past ten past two.
All right. For you.
Ten past two. Nothing burns.
And on your screen, the headline rewrites itself.
In nineteen sixty-one, the meteorologist Edward Lorenz re-ran a weather simulation, but typed in one number rounded off.
asr: In 1961, the meteorologist Edward Lawrence re-ran a weather simulation, but typed in one number rounded off.

text: Point five oh six, instead of point five oh six one two seven.
Within two simulated months, the forecast described a completely different sky.
Tomorrow is not written in stone. It bends to the smallest touch. Even yours.
That night, the worst headline yet.
Northgate Savings Bank collapses. Thousands of families lose everything they have saved.
So you warn them.
Ten shares. Then a hundred. Then a thousand.
By three in the morning, half the city has read your warning.
At dawn, they come to take their money out. All of them. At once.
In nineteen forty-eight, the sociologist Robert Merton gave this a name: the self-fulfilling prophecy.
asr: In 1948, the sociologist Robert Merton gave this a name, the self-fulfilling prophecy.

text: A false belief that makes itself come true.
A bank never keeps all its savers' money in cash. If everyone asks on the same day, it cannot pay.
In March twenty twenty-three, customers of one American bank tried to withdraw forty-two billion dollars in a single day.
asr: In March 2023, customers of one American bank tried to withdraw $42 billion in a single day.

text: By the next morning, its doors were closed.
The bank was never going to fail.
Until you told everyone it would.
Two days later, the one headline you cannot ignore.
Emergency services. What's your emergency?
The Old River Bridge. It's going to collapse at seven oh four. Close it!
asr: The Old River Bridge, it's going to collapse at 704, close it.

text: Wait. You're the courier. The one from the bank post.
Do you know how many people lost their jobs this week? Get off this line.
The Greeks told of Cassandra, a princess who could see the future, cursed so that no one would ever believe her.
Tonight, that's you.
Twenty-four minutes. Nine percent battery.
Nobody believes a warning from a stranger.
But almost everyone stops for a person standing in the road.
Stay back! Please! Stay back!
Seven oh three.
You were standing right in the road. You stopped all of us.
In the morning, your phone shows today's news. Only today's.
Nobody gets to read tomorrow.
